deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a draft of Riemann's Inaugural Dissertation (Göttingen 1851), the material of the published §§19–21 (§17 in this draft numbering). The 'Lehrsatz des vorigen Art.' is the Dirichlet-principle theorem. Take a complex function alpha+i*beta on the surface T for which the integral Omega = ∫∫[(∂α/∂x − ∂β/∂y)^2 + (∂α/∂y + ∂β/∂x)^2] dT is finite. Then there is a function u + i v, unique up to an additive constant in v, such that (alpha+i*beta) − (u+iv) is analytic, and u vanishes on the boundary. The page continues the count of data needed to determine an analytic function w = u+iv in a region.

(a) Multiply connected surface. Make the surface simply connected by q cross-cuts (Querschnitte). The theorem then yields a function determined as before, except for constant jumps across each cross-cut; in effect these are the periods of the conjugate harmonic v. The jumps can be made 0 if the boundary conditions contain q free constants. The number of constants thus equals the number of cross-cuts.

(b) A prescribed discontinuity along an interior line. Treat the line as a cut, i.e. as boundary on each of its two sides. This reduces to case (a).

(c) An isolated singular point a. By Art. 12 the only admissible violation of continuity there is the function becoming infinite. Prescribe, in a neighbourhood of a, an analytic function phi(z) (the principal part) such that w − phi is continuous at a. Then w is completely determined.

Proof sketch. Take alpha+i*beta = phi in a small disc around a. Outside, choose any admissible smooth extension meeting the boundary prescriptions. Inside the disc phi is analytic, so by the Cauchy–Riemann equations the integrand vanishes identically there. Outside, the integral is finite. Hence Omega < ∞ and the theorem applies, giving a function with the required properties (the marginal addition says exactly this).

Consequence: a pole of order n contributes the principal part sum_{k=1}^n c_k (z−a)^(−k), with n complex, i.e. 2n real, free constants.

(d) Geometric interpretation. A continuous analytic w on the region is a mapping of the plane surface T onto another surface S. It preserves connectivity and is similar in the smallest parts ('ohne Verminderung der kleinsten Theile'); this is conformality. All the determining conditions concern values of w at boundary points and singular points, hence they are conditions on the position of the boundary of S. They take two forms:
- each boundary point is constrained to a curve (a geometric locus), or
- conditions couple different parts of the boundary, so that fixing half of the mutually associated points fixes the rest.
- Mixed cases of these also occur (marginal addition).
This leads, on the following pages of the dissertation, to the Riemann mapping theorem.
errors: No mathematical error at the level of rigor intended.

The argument rests on the Dirichlet principle: existence of a minimizer of Omega, assumed without proof. Weierstrass later criticized this gap and Hilbert (1900) repaired it. This is a known gap, not a slip on this page.

Implicit (inserted by me): the extension of alpha+i*beta outside the disc must be chosen smooth and compatible with the boundary data so that the outer integral is finite. Riemann just asserts finiteness.
In case (a), the matching of the number of constants to the number of cross-cuts is asserted, not proved. Linear independence of the period conditions is not discussed.

results.what: Removal of period jumps across the q cross-cuts of a multiply connected surface by q free constants in the boundary data
results.modern_name: Periods of the harmonic conjugate on multiply connected domains; dimension count in the Dirichlet/Riemann–Hilbert problem

results.what: Existence and uniqueness of an analytic function with prescribed principal part at an isolated point, via Dirichlet principle with the local principal part as comparison function (Cauchy–Riemann makes the integrand vanish)
results.modern_name: Existence of meromorphic functions with prescribed principal parts via Dirichlet principle (Mittag-Leffler-type data on a region)

results.what: Pole of order n gives 2n real free constants
results.modern_name: Parameter count for principal parts (precursor of Riemann–Roch counting)

results.what: Analytic function as conformal mapping of surface T onto S; determining conditions become conditions on the boundary position of S
results.modern_name: Conformal mapping interpretation; prelude to Riemann mapping theorem

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of passages that appear almost verbatim in Riemann's published 1851 dissertation (§§19–21). Interest is limited to draft variants and deletions.

checkable.sympy: x,y=symbols('x y',real=True); z=x+I*y; f=1/z**2; a=re(expand_complex(f)); b=im(expand_complex(f)); simplify((diff(a,x)-diff(b,y))**2+(diff(a,y)+diff(b,x))**2)==0
checkable.asserts: For an analytic principal part (here 1/z^2) the Dirichlet-type integrand vanishes identically, so Omega over the small disc is 0.

checkable.sympy: x,y=symbols('x y',real=True); z=x+I*y; f=3/z+(2+I)/z**3; a=re(expand_complex(f)); b=im(expand_complex(f)); simplify(diff(a,x)-diff(b,y))==0 and simplify(diff(a,y)+diff(b,x))==0
checkable.asserts: Cauchy–Riemann equations hold for a general principal part of order 3; its complex coefficients c1..c3 give 6 = 2n real parameters.

transcription_corrections: Line 'ebenso wie vorhin {+bedingte+} bestimmte Function': the inserted word 'bedingte' is written above and seems to replace or qualify 'bestimmte'. Compare published 'eine bis auf ... bestimmte Function'.

'als eine Abbildung einer gegebenen ebenen Fläche S ... in eine andere S': the first surface letter is probably T, not S (published: mapping of T onto S). The interlinear 'A Grenzpuncte'/'B Grenzpuncte' readings are doubtful; they may refer to the planes A and B.
'Sie äussern entweder' is likely 'Sie bestimmen/ergeben entweder'; reading uncertain.
Margin note 'in einer Umgebung desselben' is probably 'in einer Umgebung desselben' or 'in seiner Umgebung'; the content is as transcribed.
The marginal addition reads approximately 'und so kann man dann den Lehrsatz des vorigen Art. anwenden, wodurch man eine Function mit den verlangten Eigenschaften erhält'.
